searchText: Yep, sorry for the delay, I've made quite a few changes and am in the process of testing them all. Should have a new lighthouse release soon that hopefully addresses the known lighthouse issues > <@!498009160982724610> how did you do that <https://beaconcha.in/validator/10717#overview> 100% att. effectiveness but missed attestations ;D <@!97774605351010304> I can't see the att effectiveness and not sure about what that measure is. I also lost power to my house last night, so I doubt any of my validators have been 100% effective recently ;D I'm finding these nodes: ``` 174.59.96.177:1049 167.172.133.65:9000 68.183.193.211:9000 79.142.129.218:9000 ``` In the DHT are not correctly sending back ENR responses to FINDNODE queries. Specifically, they return nodes that do not have the correct distance that was requested. I might go digging a bit later and find the client, but if you know whose these are, there's something strange with the discv5 impl it seems > <@!498009160982724610> how did you do that <https://beaconcha.in/validator/10717#overview> 100% att. effectiveness but missed attestations ;D <@!97774605351010304> This now appears. So it seems to be measured only over the last 100 epochs. So I guess in the 100 epoch window, my attestations were included quite rapidly 🙂 (strange considering I'm all the way down in Australia) ;D 😄 there are still a few bugs, so it's not that accurate yet Does 100% mean that all attestations I made were included in the immediate block? https://www.attestant.io/posts/defining-attestation-effectiveness/ if you scroll down, there is a table with examples but yes ah yep, makes sense I hacked together a short script (based on ethdo) to send voluntary exits for medalla validators, based on their launchpad keystore file: https://gist.github.com/torfbolt/3dac87d5b21eabe6e8960d811e46c04a <@!144468805697929216>
